sanskrit.iast:
parāñci khāni vyatṛṇat svayaṃbhūs tasmāt parāṅ paśyati nāntarātman |
kaścid dhīraḥ pratyag ātmānam aikṣad āvṛttacakṣur amṛtatvam icchan || 1 ||

lines.iast: parāñci khāni vyatṛṇat svayaṃbhūs tasmāt parāṅ paśyati nāntarātman
kaścid dhīraḥ pratyag ātmānam aikṣad āvṛttacakṣur amṛtatvam icchan

padaccheda.iast: parāñci khāni vyatṛṇat svayaṃbhūḥ tasmāt parāṅ paśyati na antarātman kaścit dhīraḥ pratyak ātmānam aikṣat āvṛtta-cakṣuḥ amṛta-tvam icchan
padaccheda.deva: पराञ्चि खानि व्यतृणत् स्वयंभूः तस्मात् पराङ् पश्यति न अन्तरात्मन् कश्चित् धीरः प्रत्यक् आत्मानम् ऐक्षत् आवृत्त-चक्षुः अमृत-त्वम् इच्छन्

translations.text: “The Self-existent pierced the senses so that they turn outward; therefore one sees what is outside and not the Self within. Some wise person, desiring immortality, turned his eyes back and saw the inward Self.”

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the vallī: it was said (1.3.12) that the Self, hidden in all beings, does not shine forth but is seen by a sharp understanding. What hinders that understanding? This vallī begins in order to show the cause of not seeing the Self; only when the cause that hinders the good is known can the effort to remove it begin.

Śaṅkara: khāni, ‘openings’, stands for the ear and the other senses. ‘Pierced’ means ‘injured’: the Lord made them outward-going by nature. The wise one turns them back as one would turn a river against its current. antarātman stands for antarātmānam. aikṣat, a past form, has the sense ‘sees’, tense being free in the Veda. āvṛttacakṣuḥ: with eye, ear and all the senses withdrawn from every object.

sanskrit.deva:
पराचः कामाननुयन्ति बालास्ते मृत्योर्यन्ति विततस्य पाशम् ।
अथ धीरा अमृतत्वं विदित्वा ध्रुवमध्रुवेष्विह न प्रार्थयन्ते ॥ २ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
parācaḥ kāmān anuyanti bālās te mṛtyor yanti vitatasya pāśam |
atha dhīrā amṛtatvaṃ viditvā dhruvam adhruveṣv iha na prārthayante || 2 ||

lines.iast: parācaḥ kāmān anuyanti bālās te mṛtyor yanti vitatasya pāśam
lines.deva: पराचः कामाननुयन्ति बालास्ते मृत्योर्यन्ति विततस्य पाशम्

lines.iast: atha dhīrā amṛtatvaṃ viditvā dhruvam adhruveṣv iha na prārthayante
lines.deva: अथ धीरा अमृतत्वं विदित्वा ध्रुवमध्रुवेष्विह न प्रार्थयन्ते

padaccheda.iast: parācaḥ kāmān anuyanti bālāḥ te mṛtyoḥ yanti vitatasya pāśam atha dhīrāḥ amṛta-tvam viditvā dhruvam adhruveṣu iha na prārthayante
padaccheda.deva: पराचः कामान् अनुयन्ति बालाः ते मृत्योः यन्ति विततस्य पाशम् अथ धीराः अमृत-त्वम् विदित्वा ध्रुवम् अध्रुवेषु इह न प्रार्थयन्ते

grammar.en: past passive participle m. gen. sg.

translations.text: “The childish follow outward objects of desire, and they walk into the widespread snare of death. The wise, therefore, having known immortality as the one stable thing, ask for nothing here among things that are unstable.”

notes: Śaṅkara: death here is the whole of ignorance, desire and action; its snare is union with body and senses, that is, the unbroken run of birth, death, old age and disease. The stable immortality is abiding in one's nature as the inward Self. The wise rise above the desire for sons, wealth and worlds.

sanskrit.deva:
येन रूपं रसं गन्धं शब्दान्स्पर्शांश्च मैथुनान् ।
एतेनैव विजानाति किमत्र परिशिष्यते ।
एतद्वै तत् ॥ ३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yena rūpaṃ rasaṃ gandhaṃ śabdān sparśāṃśca maithunān |
etenaiva vijānāti kim atra pariśiṣyate |
etad vai tat || 3 ||

lines.iast: yena rūpaṃ rasaṃ gandhaṃ śabdān sparśāṃśca maithunān
lines.deva: येन रूपं रसं गन्धं शब्दान्स्पर्शांश्च मैथुनान्

lines.iast: etenaiva vijānāti kim atra pariśiṣyate
etad vai tat

padaccheda.iast: yena rūpam rasam gandham śabdān sparśān ca maithunān etena eva vijānāti kim atra pariśiṣyate etat vai tat
padaccheda.deva: येन रूपम् रसम् गन्धम् शब्दान् स्पर्शान् च मैथुनान् एतेन एव विजानाति किम् अत्र परिशिष्यते एतत् वै तत्

translations.text: “That by which one knows form, taste, smell, sounds, touches and the pleasures of union: by this alone one knows. What remains here unknown to it? This indeed is that.”

notes: Śaṅkara: it is the Self, whose nature is consciousness. The body and the rest, being themselves made of form and the like and being objects of knowledge, cannot be the knower; one knows them through the Self that is distinct from them, as that by which iron burns is fire. Nothing is left that the Self does not know: it is all-knowing.

Śaṅkara: etad vai tat: this is that which Naciketas asked about, which even the gods doubted, which is other than righteousness and the rest: the highest state of Viṣṇu, beyond which there is nothing.

sanskrit.deva:
स्वप्नान्तं जागरितान्तं चोभौ येनानुपश्यति ।
महान्तं विभुमात्मानं मत्वा धीरो न शोचति ॥ ४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
svapnāntaṃ jāgaritāntaṃ cobhau yenānupaśyati |
mahāntaṃ vibhum ātmānaṃ matvā dhīro na śocati || 4 ||

lines.iast: svapnāntaṃ jāgaritāntaṃ cobhau yenānupaśyati
mahāntaṃ vibhum ātmānaṃ matvā dhīro na śocati
lines.deva: महान्तं विभुमात्मानं मत्वा धीरो न शोचति

padaccheda.iast: svapna-antam jāgarita-antam ca ubhau yena anupaśyati mahāntam vibhum ātmānam matvā dhīraḥ na śocati
padaccheda.deva: स्वप्न-अन्तम् जागरित-अन्तम् च उभौ येन अनुपश्यति महान्तम् विभुम् आत्मानम् मत्वा धीरः न शोचति

translations.text: “That by which one perceives both what is seen in dream and what is seen in waking: knowing that great, all-pervading Self, the wise man does not grieve.”

notes: Śaṅkara: because the Self is so subtle and hard to know, the same thing is said again and again. svapnānta: what lies within dream, the objects known in dream. He knows it directly as ‘I am the supreme Self’.

sanskrit.deva:
य इमं मध्वदं वेद आत्मानं जीवमन्तिकात् ।
ईशानं भूतभव्यस्य न ततो विजुगुप्सते ।
एतद्वै तत् ॥ ५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ya imaṃ madhvadaṃ veda ātmānaṃ jīvam antikāt |
īśānaṃ bhūtabhavyasya na tato vijugupsate |
etad vai tat || 5 ||

lines.iast: ya imaṃ madhvadaṃ veda ātmānaṃ jīvam antikāt
lines.deva: य इमं मध्वदं वेद आत्मानं जीवमन्तिकात्

lines.iast: īśānaṃ bhūtabhavyasya na tato vijugupsate
etad vai tat

padaccheda.iast: yaḥ imam madhvadam veda ātmānam jīvam antikāt īśānam bhūta-bhavyasya na tataḥ vijugupsate etat vai tat
padaccheda.deva: यः इमम् मध्वदम् वेद आत्मानम् जीवम् अन्तिकात् ईशानम् भूत-भव्यस्य न ततः विजुगुप्सते एतत् वै तत्

words.meaning: of what has been and what is to be

translations.text: “He who knows this Self, the eater of honey, the living one, close at hand, as the lord of what has been and what is to be, no longer seeks to protect himself. This indeed is that.”

notes: Śaṅkara: madhvada: the one who tastes the fruits of action; jīva: the sustainer of the life-breaths. ‘Lord of past and future’ covers the three times. As long as a man thinks himself impermanent and exposed to fear, he wishes to guard himself; once he knows the Self as eternal and without a second, who would guard what, and from what?
vijugupsate is a desiderative form; it is labelled here as a present.

sanskrit.deva:
यः पूर्वं तपसो जातमद्भ्यः पूर्वमजायत ।
गुहां प्रविश्य तिष्ठन्तं यो भूतेभिर्व्यपश्यत ।
एतद्वै तत् ॥ ६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yaḥ pūrvaṃ tapaso jātam adbhyaḥ pūrvam ajāyata |
guhāṃ praviśya tiṣṭhantaṃ yo bhūtebhir vyapaśyata |
etad vai tat || 6 ||

lines.iast: yaḥ pūrvaṃ tapaso jātam adbhyaḥ pūrvam ajāyata
guhāṃ praviśya tiṣṭhantaṃ yo bhūtebhir vyapaśyata
etad vai tat

padaccheda.iast: yaḥ pūrvam tapasaḥ jātam adbhyaḥ pūrvam ajāyata guhām praviśya tiṣṭhantam yaḥ bhūtebhiḥ vyapaśyata etat vai tat
padaccheda.deva: यः पूर्वम् तपसः जातम् अद्भ्यः पूर्वम् अजायत गुहाम् प्रविश्य तिष्ठन्तम् यः भूतेभिः व्यपश्यत एतत् वै तत्

grammar.en: past passive participle m. acc. sg.

translations.text: “He who sees the first-born, born of old from austerity, born before the waters, who has entered the cave and abides there with the elements: he sees this very Brahman. This indeed is that.”

notes: Śaṅkara: the inward Self, already shown to be the Lord, is now shown to be the Self of all. The first-born is Hiraṇyagarbha, born from Brahman, whose austerity is knowledge. ‘Before the waters’ means before all five elements, water included. The cave is the space in the heart of every creature; the bhūtas are the body and organs. bhūtebhiḥ is the Vedic form of bhūtaiḥ. vyapaśyata has the sense ‘sees’.

Śaṅkara: etad vai tat: this is that which Naciketas asked about, which even the gods doubted, which is other than righteousness and the rest: the highest state of Viṣṇu, beyond which there is nothing.

sanskrit.deva:
या प्राणेन सम्भवति अदितिर्देवतामयी ।
गुहां प्रविश्य तिष्ठन्तीं या भूतेभिर्व्यजायत ।
एतद्वै तत् ॥ ७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yā prāṇena sambhavati aditir devatāmayī |
guhāṃ praviśya tiṣṭhantīṃ yā bhūtebhir vyajāyata |
etad vai tat || 7 ||

lines.iast: yā prāṇena sambhavati aditir devatāmayī
guhāṃ praviśya tiṣṭhantīṃ yā bhūtebhir vyajāyata
etad vai tat

padaccheda.iast: yā prāṇena sambhavati aditiḥ devatā-mayī guhām praviśya tiṣṭhantīm yā bhūtebhiḥ vyajāyata etat vai tat
padaccheda.deva: या प्राणेन सम्भवति अदितिः देवता-मयी गुहाम् प्रविश्य तिष्ठन्तीम् या भूतेभिः व्यजायत एतत् वै तत्

translations.text: “She who arises as the life-breath, Aditi, made of all the gods, who has entered the cave and abides there, who was born together with the elements: this indeed is that.”

notes: Śaṅkara: she arises from the supreme Brahman in the form of Hiraṇyagarbha, the life-breath. She is called Aditi because she ‘eats’ (adana) sound and the other objects.

Śaṅkara: etad vai tat: this is that which Naciketas asked about, which even the gods doubted, which is other than righteousness and the rest: the highest state of Viṣṇu, beyond which there is nothing.

sanskrit.deva:
अरण्योर्निहितो जातवेदा गर्भ इव सुभृतो गर्भिणीभिः ।
दिवे दिव ईड्यो जागृवद्भिर्हविष्मद्भिर्मनुष्येभिरग्निः ।
एतद्वै तत् ॥ ८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
araṇyor nihito jātavedā garbha iva subhṛto garbhiṇībhiḥ |
dive diva īḍyo jāgṛvadbhir haviṣmadbhir manuṣyebhir agniḥ |
etad vai tat || 8 ||

lines.iast: araṇyor nihito jātavedā garbha iva subhṛto garbhiṇībhiḥ
lines.deva: अरण्योर्निहितो जातवेदा गर्भ इव सुभृतो गर्भिणीभिः

lines.iast: dive diva īḍyo jāgṛvadbhir haviṣmadbhir manuṣyebhir agniḥ
etad vai tat

padaccheda.iast: araṇyoḥ nihitaḥ jātavedāḥ garbhaḥ iva su-bhṛtaḥ garbhiṇībhiḥ dive dive īḍyaḥ jāgṛvadbhiḥ haviṣmadbhiḥ manuṣyebhiḥ agniḥ etat vai tat
padaccheda.deva: अरण्योः निहितः जातवेदाः गर्भः इव सु-भृतः गर्भिणीभिः दिवे दिवे ईड्यः जागृवद्भिः हविष्मद्भिः मनुष्येभिः अग्निः एतत् वै तत्

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. sg.

translations.text: “The fire lodged in the two fire-sticks, well cared for as an unborn child is by pregnant women, and to be praised day after day by wakeful men who bring offerings: this indeed is that.”

notes: Śaṅkara: in the sacrifice it is the fire kept in the upper and lower fire-sticks, the consumer of all offerings; within the person it is tended in the heart by yogīs. ‘Wakeful’: vigilant; the offerings are clarified butter and the like for the ritualist, and meditation for the yogī. manuṣyebhiḥ is the Vedic form of manuṣyaiḥ.

Śaṅkara: etad vai tat: this is that which Naciketas asked about, which even the gods doubted, which is other than righteousness and the rest: the highest state of Viṣṇu, beyond which there is nothing.

sanskrit.deva:
यतश्चोदेति सूर्यो अस्तं यत्र च गच्छति ।
तं देवाः सर्वे अर्पितास्तदु नात्येति कश्चन ।
एतद्वै तत् ॥ ९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yataś codeti sūryo astaṃ yatra ca gacchati |
taṃ devāḥ sarve arpitās tad u nātyeti kaścana |
etad vai tat || 9 ||

lines.iast: yataś codeti sūryo astaṃ yatra ca gacchati
lines.deva: यतश्चोदेति सूर्यो अस्तं यत्र च गच्छति

lines.iast: taṃ devāḥ sarve arpitās tad u nātyeti kaścana
lines.deva: तं देवाः सर्वे अर्पितास्तदु नात्येति कश्चन

lines.iast: etad vai tat

padaccheda.iast: yataḥ ca udeti sūryaḥ astam yatra ca gacchati tam devāḥ sarve arpitāḥ tat u na atyeti kaścana etat vai tat
padaccheda.deva: यतः च उदेति सूर्यः अस्तम् यत्र च गच्छति तम् देवाः सर्वे अर्पिताः तत् उ न अत्येति कश्चन एतत् वै तत्

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. pl.

translations.text: “That from which the sun rises and in which it sets: in that all the gods are fixed, and no one goes beyond it. This indeed is that.”

notes: Śaṅkara: ‘that’ is the life-breath, the Self. The gods are fire and the rest in the cosmos, and speech and the rest in the person; they are fixed in it like spokes in the hub of a wheel. It too is Brahman, the Self of all. No one, ceasing to be of its nature, becomes other than it.

Śaṅkara: etad vai tat: this is that which Naciketas asked about, which even the gods doubted, which is other than righteousness and the rest: the highest state of Viṣṇu, beyond which there is nothing.

sanskrit.deva:
यदेवेह तदमुत्र यदमुत्र तदन्विह ।
मृत्योः स मृत्युमाप्नोति य इह नानेव पश्यति ॥ १० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yad eveha tad amutra yad amutra tad anv iha |
mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyum āpnoti ya iha nāneva paśyati || 10 ||

lines.iast: yad eveha tad amutra yad amutra tad anv iha
mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyum āpnoti ya iha nāneva paśyati
lines.deva: मृत्योः स मृत्युमाप्नोति य इह नानेव पश्यति

padaccheda.iast: yat eva iha tat amutra yat amutra tat anu iha mṛtyoḥ saḥ mṛtyum āpnoti yaḥ iha nānā iva paśyati
padaccheda.deva: यत् एव इह तत् अमुत्र यत् अमुत्र तत् अनु इह मृत्योः सः मृत्युम् आप्नोति यः इह नाना इव पश्यति

translations.text: “What is here, that is there; what is there, that again is here. He goes from death to death who sees here any seeming difference.”

notes: Śaṅkara: this removes the doubt that the self in beings, from Brahmā down to plants, is other than the supreme Brahman. ‘Here’: joined to the adjuncts of body and organs, and appearing to the undiscerning to have the properties of the cycle of birth and death. ‘There’: established in itself, by nature unbroken consciousness. One who thinks ‘I am other than the supreme, and Brahman is other than I’ comes to birth and death again and again.

sanskrit.deva:
मनसैवेदमाप्तव्यं नेह नानास्ति किंचन ।
मृत्योः स मृत्युं गच्छति य इह नानेव पश्यति ॥ ११ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
manasaivedam āptavyaṃ neha nānāsti kiṃcana |
mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyuṃ gacchati ya iha nāneva paśyati || 11 ||

lines.iast: manasaivedam āptavyaṃ neha nānāsti kiṃcana
mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyuṃ gacchati ya iha nāneva paśyati
lines.deva: मृत्योः स मृत्युं गच्छति य इह नानेव पश्यति

padaccheda.iast: manasā eva idam āptavyam na iha nānā asti kiṃcana mṛtyoḥ saḥ mṛtyum gacchati yaḥ iha nānā iva paśyati
padaccheda.deva: मनसा एव इदम् आप्तव्यम् न इह नाना अस्ति किंचन मृत्योः सः मृत्युम् गच्छति यः इह नाना इव पश्यति

translations.text: “By the mind alone is this to be attained: there is no difference here at all. He goes from death to death who sees here any seeming difference.”

notes: Śaṅkara: by a mind made ready by teacher and scripture. Once it is attained, the ignorance that sets up difference is gone, and not the least trace of difference remains in Brahman.

sanskrit.deva:
अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषो मध्य आत्मनि तिष्ठति ।
ईशानो भूतभव्यस्य न ततो विजुगुप्सते ।
एतद्वै तत् ॥ १२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo madhya ātmani tiṣṭhati |
īśāno bhūtabhavyasya na tato vijugupsate |
etad vai tat || 12 ||

lines.iast: aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo madhya ātmani tiṣṭhati
īśāno bhūtabhavyasya na tato vijugupsate
etad vai tat

padaccheda.iast: aṅguṣṭha-mātraḥ puruṣaḥ madhye ātmani tiṣṭhati īśānaḥ bhūta-bhavyasya na tataḥ vijugupsate etat vai tat
padaccheda.deva: अङ्गुष्ठ-मात्रः पुरुषः मध्ये आत्मनि तिष्ठति ईशानः भूत-भव्यस्य न ततः विजुगुप्सते एतत् वै तत्

words.meaning: of what has been and what is to be

translations.text: “The Person, the size of a thumb, dwells in the middle of the body, the lord of what has been and what is to be. Knowing him, one no longer seeks to protect oneself. This indeed is that.”

notes: Śaṅkara: the lotus of the heart is the size of a thumb; limited by the inner organ that lies in its hollow, the Self is called ‘the size of a thumb’, like the space inside a thumb-length joint of bamboo. puruṣa: by him all this is filled. ātmani here means ‘in the body’.

Śaṅkara: etad vai tat: this is that which Naciketas asked about, which even the gods doubted, which is other than righteousness and the rest: the highest state of Viṣṇu, beyond which there is nothing.

sanskrit.deva:
अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषो ज्योतिरिव अधूमकः ।
ईशानो भूतभव्यस्य स एवाद्य स उ श्वः ।
एतद्वै तत् ॥ १३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo jyotir iva adhūmakaḥ |
īśāno bhūtabhavyasya sa evādya sa u śvaḥ |
etad vai tat || 13 ||

lines.iast: aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo jyotir iva adhūmakaḥ
īśāno bhūtabhavyasya sa evādya sa u śvaḥ
lines.deva: ईशानो भूतभव्यस्य स एवाद्य स उ श्वः

lines.iast: etad vai tat

padaccheda.iast: aṅguṣṭha-mātraḥ puruṣaḥ jyotiḥ iva adhūmakaḥ īśānaḥ bhūta-bhavyasya saḥ eva adya saḥ u śvaḥ etat vai tat
padaccheda.deva: अङ्गुष्ठ-मात्रः पुरुषः ज्योतिः इव अधूमकः ईशानः भूत-भव्यस्य सः एव अद्य सः उ श्वः एतत् वै तत्

words.meaning: of what has been and what is to be

translations.text: “The Person, the size of a thumb, is like a flame without smoke, the lord of what has been and what is to be. He alone is today, and he will be tomorrow. This indeed is that.”

notes: Śaṅkara: the one thus perceived in the heart by yogīs is eternal and unchanging: present in beings now, he will be so tomorrow, and no other like him will be born. In its own words the Upaniṣad here sets aside the view ‘he does not exist’ (1.1.20), and also the doctrine that everything is momentary.

Śaṅkara: etad vai tat: this is that which Naciketas asked about, which even the gods doubted, which is other than righteousness and the rest: the highest state of Viṣṇu, beyond which there is nothing.

sanskrit.deva:
यथोदकं दुर्गे वृष्टं पर्वतेषु विधावति ।
एवं धर्मान्पृथक्पश्यंस्तानेवानु विधावति ॥ १४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yathodakaṃ durge vṛṣṭaṃ parvateṣu vidhāvati |
evaṃ dharmān pṛthak paśyaṃs tān evānu vidhāvati || 14 ||

lines.iast: yathodakaṃ durge vṛṣṭaṃ parvateṣu vidhāvati
evaṃ dharmān pṛthak paśyaṃs tān evānu vidhāvati

padaccheda.iast: yathā udakam durge vṛṣṭam parvateṣu vidhāvati evam dharmān pṛthak paśyan tān eva anu vidhāvati
padaccheda.deva: यथा उदकम् दुर्गे वृष्टम् पर्वतेषु विधावति एवम् धर्मान् पृथक् पश्यन् तान् एव अनु विधावति

words.meaning: on a height hard to reach

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: “As water rained on a height runs off among the hills and is lost, so one who sees the selves as separate runs after them alone.”

notes: anu … vidhāvati is one verb (anuvidhāvati), its parts separated in the verse.

Śaṅkara: the dharmas here are selves, which are not different from the Self; one who sees them as separate in each body keeps taking on one separate body after another. The water, scattered over the low ground, is lost.

sanskrit.deva:
यथोदकं शुद्धे शुद्धमासिक्तं तादृगेव भवति ।
एवं मुनेर्विजानत आत्मा भवति गौतम ॥ १५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yathodakaṃ śuddhe śuddham āsiktaṃ tādṛg eva bhavati |
evaṃ muner vijānata ātmā bhavati gautama || 15 ||

lines.iast: yathodakaṃ śuddhe śuddham āsiktaṃ tādṛg eva bhavati
evaṃ muner vijānata ātmā bhavati gautama

padaccheda.iast: yathā udakam śuddhe śuddham āsiktam tādṛk eva bhavati evam muneḥ vijānataḥ ātmā bhavati gautama
padaccheda.deva: यथा उदकम् शुद्धे शुद्धम् आसिक्तम् तादृक् एव भवति एवम् मुनेः विजानतः आत्मा भवति गौतम

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: “As pure water poured into pure water becomes just the same, so becomes the Self of the sage who knows, O Gautama.”

notes: Śaṅkara: for the sage, the reflective one, who has cast off the seeing of difference made by adjuncts and knows the oneness of the Self, the Self is of one nature only. Therefore the vision of oneness taught by the Veda, a better friend than a thousand mothers and fathers, is to be honoured.
